behaviorChanges: session-start surfaces (lane-start, sync-methodology, methodology-status) report the genuinely available framework version and a non-blocking `framework_update_offer:` line naming the FIRST real unblock (trust-aware: pinned -> update-repin then sync; signed/experimental -> sync; stable+untrusted -> the full trust chain), instead of the silent `methodology_update: skipped`. Display-only: no update policy, trust gate, auto-advance, or exit-code changes; framework_update_decision and framework_available_version are byte-identical.

a read-only, fail-open, cached update probe (`~/.cache/tautline/update-probe.json`) discovers the available version via a single `ls-remote` per launch; launches never fetch. Opt out with `TAUTLINE_METHODOLOGY_UPDATE_PROBE=off`. Any probe failure yields byte-identical session-start output to before.

methodology-status (only, and only without --no-remote) performs one bounded fetch into a disposable `refs/tautline-update-probe/*` ref + FETCH_HEAD to resolve a not-yet-local candidate's version; it never touches HEAD, the working tree, the index, or the branch tracking ref, and currency stays HEAD-based.

requiredMigrations.command: gh auth refresh --hostname github.com -s read:project -s project
requiredMigrations.description: Carried forward from 0.10.3 for lanes updating across it: grant the gh token the GitHub Projects scopes the fail-closed board gates need. Machines already on 0.10.3+ or whose token carries read:project and project need no action.

rollbackNotes: Repinning below 0.14.4 removes the update-availability/offer lines and the probe; the silent `methodology_update: skipped` behavior returns. No state migration: the probe cache and the disposable probe ref are inert and can be deleted.
grant-gh-project-scopes is carried forward from 0.10.3 (see requiredMigrations); a lane already on 0.10.3+ needs no action.
NOT WIP-safe only for the engine-gap carry-forward; the release's own change is display-only and safe for lanes in progress.
